STJ Home
Welcome to St John’s Marlborough
Set in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty on Granham Hill, St John’s Marlborough is where young people aged 11-18 are challenged and supported to become confident, capable adults ready for their next steps in life.
We’re proud to serve the communities of Marlborough and surrounding villages with a relentless focus on high aspirations and outstanding outcomes for every student. Our state-of-the-art facilities provide an exceptional learning environment, whilst our distinct and ambitious Sixth Form welcomes both existing students and those joining us from other schools.
As part of Excalibur Academies Trust, we benefit from shared expertise and strong governance, whilst maintaining our own unique identity, values and deep community focus.
We look forward to welcoming you to our school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision and Values - St John's Marlborough
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
Our Vision and Values
At St John’s, our vision is to foster a positive, inclusive, and ambitious learning culture where every student and member of staff is supported and challenged to achieve their very best. We are committed to nurturing a community built on high expectations, mutual respect, and a shared belief in the potential of every individual. Through strong relationships, purposeful learning, and a culture that celebrates growth, we empower our students to thrive academically, personally, and socially.
Ambition
Ambition – Striving for Excellence
We dream big, set goals and work hard to achieve them. We believe in our potential and strive for excellence.
Ambition is the path to success; persistence is the vehicle you arrive in.
Integrity
Integrity – Doing What’s Right
We are honest, responsible and true to our word. We do what is right, even when it’s not easy.
Integrity is doing the right thing, even when no one is watching
Respect
Respect – Action With Kindness
We value every individual and celebrate our differences. We listen, support and treat others with kindness.
Respect is the foundation of strong relationships.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Principal
Welcome from the Principal
Welcome to St John’s Marlborough.
At St John’s, we are proud to be a community where every student is valued and where ambition, integrity, and respect shape all that we do. We hold high aspirations for every young person who walks through our doors, believing deeply in their potential to thrive. Each student is welcomed with dignity and treated with genuine respect, and we work hard to create an environment rich in opportunity, challenge, and support.
We recognise our responsibility to prepare students for a world that demands resilience, independence, and strong moral character. From the earliest stages, we nurture these qualities, encouraging students to discover their strengths, develop new talents, and celebrate the diverse qualities of those around them. Our reputation as a caring Academy with high academic standards and a disciplined, purposeful atmosphere is one we cherish and continually strive to enhance.
Truly great schools excel in the fundamentals, and the quality of education at St John’s remains at the heart of our mission. Alongside excellent teaching and learning, we place great importance on the values that shape responsible citizens: respect for others, integrity in conduct, care for the environment, and pride in personal presentation. We know that wellbeing underpins achievement, so we ensure that every student is supported to lead a healthy, happy, and fulfilling life.
The world our students are growing into is demanding, both within school and beyond. By choosing St John’s, you are choosing a school that takes this responsibility seriously and embraces it with ambition and care. I hope you enjoy exploring our website and gaining a sense of the opportunities and experiences we offer. We would be delighted to welcome you into our school so you can see first-hand the vibrant, respectful, and aspirational community your child could be part of.
Alan Henderson Principal

pageCache.pageTitle: Art & Design Curriculum - St John's Marlborough
pageCache.text:
Art & Design Curriculum
Art & Design Curriculum
Welcome
Aims: The Art and Design curriculum at St Johns gives all students the opportunity to realise their potential in creating, presenting and appreciating art. All students have access to a wide range of experiences and will be encouraged to become independent, confident learners with a sound knowledge of how materials can be used, how artists can inspire us and how art can lead to a variety of careers.
Aims: The Photography curriculum enables students to understand the world around them through observation, questioning and by responding to their environment. We want students to be exposed to, and learn to appreciate and understand, photography. Students will be equipped to be strong visual communicators, prepared for the workplace with a skill set based on time management, problem solving and lateral thinking skills.
Art & Design Department Staff
Head of Expressive Arts Faculty: Mrs L Spokes Head of Art Department: Ms E O’Brien Key Stage 3 Subject Lead: Mrs E Tin Arts Award Coordinator: Mrs Rachel Coupland

pageCache.pageTitle: Classical Civilisations & Latin - St John's Marlborough
pageCache.text:
Classical Civilisations & Latin
Classical Civilisations & Latin
Welcome
Aims: The Classics curriculum will equip students with the knowledge of the ancient Classical world, focusing on ancient Greek and Roman literature and culture. Students will be able to analyse and evaluate primary source material, using this to form their own opinions on key Classical topics. We aim to foster a love of the ancient world, allowing the students to fully access the curriculum and encourage uptake for KS4, KS5 and beyond.
Aims: The Latin curriculum will allow students to develop their understanding of the Latin language and the related ancient literature, values and society. Students will be able to look at Latin passages, analyse vocabulary and syntax, and make links to English and other modern foreign languages. We aim to foster a love of the ancient world, allowing the students to fully access the curriculum and encourage uptake for KS4, KS5 and beyond.
Classics Department Staff
Subject Leader for Classics & Latin: Miss S Thomas

English & Media Curriculum
English & Media Curriculum
Welcome
Aims: The St John’s English curriculum aims to empower students to use, understand and explore language to express themselves and make sense of the world around them. We aim to equip students with a solid foundation of knowledge and lifelong skills in reading, writing and oracy. In doing so we hope to foster a love of reading and inspire students to adopt a critical eye towards any texts they may experience.
English & Media Department Staff

History Curriculum
Welcome
Aims: The History curriculum at St John’s ensures that students are prepared for the complex world of information today, and understand how to evaluate it effectively. Students are encouraged to synthesise this knowledge and to construct and present effective arguments. We examine a variety of cultures, societies and times in order to develop students’ sense of empathy and prepare them for a multicultural world. We enrich students’ learning through immersion in the historical environment, through analysis of evidence, a range of trips and visits, and we aim to foster a love for the subject.
History Department Staff

Design & Technology Curriculum
Design & Technology Curriculum
Welcome
Aims: The Design & Technology curriculum aim is to prepare St John’s students to participate confidently and successfully in an increasingly technological world, through exploration of the world of creative and original design. Design and Technology is where Art and Science meet, and students will explore a wide range of design materials and to use them creatively, designing and making products using a range of new technologies. The curriculum will facilitate progression through GCSE, A level and on to University.

Music Tuition (Private)
Music Tuition (Private)
Private Music Tuition at St John’s Marlborough
Private teachers provide the instrumental tuition at St John’s. Tuition fees for lessons are not set by St John’s and are paid directly to the individual teachers according to their usual rates. All students should have their own instrument. Pianos and drum kits are provided.
Lessons are given during school hours (making maximum use of breaks and lunchtime) and are organised on a rota basis so that students do not miss the same lesson each week. Sixth Form students may be able to use their study periods. Students are responsible for catching up with work missed. Students have the opportunity to take ABRSM, Trinity and Rockschool examinations depending on the instrument and teacher.
Students are encouraged to take part in one of the many music ensembles on offer, including the School Orchestra, Jazz Band, Training Band, String Ensemble, Brass Ensemble, Woodwind Group and Choirs as well as student-led groups. There are a number of performance opportunities during the year including multiple evening concerts, the Christmas Carol Concert at St Mary’s, the annual school production and the Savernake and Stedman Cup competitions.
The music department includes two teaching classrooms, one equipped with a full Mac suite, an ensemble room for rehearsals, a recording studio and a number of practice rooms where instrumental music lessons are taught.

Welcome to St John’s Marlborough
Set in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty on Granham Hill, St John’s Marlborough is where young people aged 11-18 are challenged and supported to become confident, capable adults ready for their next steps in life.
We’re proud to serve the communities of Marlborough and surrounding villages with a relentless focus on high aspirations and outstanding outcomes for every student. Our state-of-the-art facilities provide an exceptional learning environment, whilst our distinct and ambitious Sixth Form welcomes both existing students and those joining us from other schools.
As part of Excalibur Academies Trust, we benefit from shared expertise and strong governance, whilst maintaining our own unique identity, values and deep community focus.
We look forward to welcoming you to our school community.

pageCache.text:
SEND and Inclusion
SEND and Inclusion
Supporting Every Child to Thrive
At St John’s Marlborough, we are committed to ensuring that every student, regardless of their needs, receives the support they deserve to thrive academically, socially, and personally.
Our approach to Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) is built on a foundation of high-quality, inclusive teaching, with additional targeted support available when needed.
Our Three Levels of Support
Every student at St John’s benefits from high-quality, inclusive teaching in every lesson.
Our teachers use adaptive teaching strategies to ensure that all learners can access the curriculum and make progress. This universal offer forms the foundation of our inclusive approach and is available to every child in our school.
Classroom Strategies Classroom strategies might include breaking tasks down into small steps, using clear models and demonstrations, or providing alternative ways to record information such as diagrams.
For many children, these everyday classroom adaptations provide all the support they need to fully access learning in lessons.
Graduated Response We use our graduated response to monitor every child’s progress through a cycle of “assess, plan, do, review”, where we can continually adapt and tailor strategies to address learners’ needs.
More information about our Universal Offer.
Examples of Adaptive Teaching Practices
When students need additional help beyond our universal offer, we provide targeted interventions.
This may include support from teaching assistants, small group work, specific learning programmes, or access to Learning and Support – a dedicated space where students can receive focused support.
For students receiving targeted support, we work closely with parents to create a One-Page Profile that clearly sets out the interventions and strategies in place.
For students with the most complex needs, we provide specialist support through carefully designed provision packages.
This may include support from educational psychologists, speech and language therapists, or other specialists, and is underpinned by an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) where appropriate.
Our Commitment
Every member of staff at St John’s Marlborough is committed to supporting positive outcomes for students with SEND.
Our dedicated SEND team works alongside classroom teachers to ensure that the right support is in place at the right time.
We believe in working in partnership with parents and carers, and we welcome your involvement in planning and reviewing your child’s support.
If you have any questions about SEND provision at St John’s Marlborough, or would like to discuss your child’s needs, please contact us at send@stjohns.excalibur.org.uk.
Our SEND Team
Mrs K Room – Assistant Vice Principal, Inclusion Operations Mrs S Cardy – Statutory SENDCO Mr C Walker – Assistant SENCO Ms L Anthistle – SEND Administrator and Access Arrangements Coordinator Mrs K Skiffington – Teaching Assistant Manager Mrs J Stevens – SEND Governor
You can contact our SEND team at send@stjohns.excalibur.org.uk .
Support for Parents
If your child is joining St John’s, we will work with you and their previous school or setting to understand your child’s needs. We’ll gather information about what works for them and how we can best support them.
All students have transition visits, and we can arrange additional visits if needed. We also offer guided tours for in-year transfers and prospective families who have a child in Year six..
EHCP If your child has an EHCP, your Local Authority SEND Lead Worker will consult with St John’s to secure your child’s place. This should be done following your child’s Year 5 Transition Annual Review.
FAQs We have put together a list of the most frequently asked questions from previous Year 5/6 open evenings. SEND FAQs
We proactively review every child’s progress through standardised assessments (e.g. CATS, NGRT reading tests), Curriculum Impact Assessments (CIAs) and ongoing teacher observation and assessment, all of which are helpful in identifying possible needs.
Graduated Approach We use a graduated approach comprising four stages: assess, plan, do and review to highlight where children may need additional support beyond our universal offer.
Identifying SEND Needs and Diagnosis We are unable to diagnose a specific SEN in school, but we can identify needs and put in place approaches to support them. It is not necessary for a child to have a formal diagnosis to receive SEN support.
If you are unsure whether a formal diagnosis is right for your child and want more information about the options open to you, please see the following document: SEND – Identifying Needs and Formal Diagnosis.
Test Assistance and Access Arrangements help schools to offer equal opportunities to students with additional needs during tests and exams.
The main difference between these two support measures are: • Test Assistance: offered by teachers in accordance with the student’s daily needs. • Access Arrangements: in place as a legal requirement from KS4 onwards to enable students to access assessments in compliance with the Equality Act 2010.
Students are assessed for Access Arrangements based on teacher observation and identification of need. There are very strict eligibility criteria which are subject to regulation and overseen by the Joint Council of Qualifications.
We are committed to providing a fully accessible environment which values and includes all pupils, staff, parents and visitors and our buildings are designed to promote physical accessibility. You can find full details of how our site is accessible in our Accessibility Plan.
If you are worried or anxious about your child’s progress or wellbeing at St John’s, it is best to approach their tutor, subject teacher or key worker first. Our switchboard number is 01672 516156, or you can email us at enquiries@stjohns.excalibur.org.uk.
The SEND team will contact you to discuss your child’s progress at various points throughout the year, either in-person, by telephone or online.
We will work with you to regularly review any One Page Profile that may be in place for your child, and welcome feedback on the support we have put in place. If you need support in the interim, you can contact us at send@stjohns.excalibur.org.uk
If you have feedback on your child’s One Page Profile, or want to update us on any changes, please contact us using our Parent Feedback Form.
We will respond to all queries as soon as possible and always within 5 working days as outlined in our Communication Policy.

ClassCharts
ClassCharts
We are delighted to provide information for our exciting Attendance, Behaviour and Homework application – Class Charts.
Parental Access to Class Charts
Class Charts for parents can be accessed via a website, or iOS and Android apps. The three links the the first row of buttons below will enable you to access Class Charts either through your browser or using an app.
How do I register?
If you haven’t already downloaded the app for your phone, see relevant app store in the buttons below and download the appropriate ClassCharts app. Alternatively, you can opt to use the browser on your phone.
To register, your unique parent code will be sent to you. This code is used to set up your parent account. The code can be shared between parents/carers as an account can be created with separate email addresses. If you have a child in Year 7, Your child will be taught how to set up and use their Class Charts in their first few IT lessons.
Once on the Class Charts website or in the app, click “I don’t have an account yet”. You will then need to input your personal email address, your parent code, your child’s name and date of birth, plus a password of your choice. Once this in entered, just click login. This will generate an automatic email to your personal email and supply a verification code that you will need to enter. Please do check your junk or spam folder for this email. Once you have verified your email address, you will be able to login to Class Charts using your personal email and chosen password. You will be able to set up push notifications from the mobile applications.
There is a “forgot password” facility within the website and application to reset your password if you need to do so in the future.
We hope that you find Class Charts is a valuable application that will enable you to be more engaged with your child’s education.

Medical Matters
Medical Matters
Medical Needs Information
St John’s is an inclusive community and understands it has a responsibility to welcome and support current and future students who have additional medical needs. We aim to provide all students with medical conditions the same opportunities as others at school. We will help to ensure they can:
The Medical Conditions Policy along with all other relevant policies are available on our Academy Policies (in the About Us menu above left) and includes the following:
If you would like to discuss your child’s condition and additional needs, please contact our First Aider Gillian Deery on 01672 517835 or STJFirstAid@stjohns.excalibur.org.uk.
be healthy
stay safe
enjoy and achieve
make a positive contribution
achieve economic well-being
Medication for Students
Non-prescribed medication
Sometimes students may request or require pain relief (analgesics) at school e.g. Paracetamol or Ibuprofen. Generally, school staff will not give non-prescribed medication to pupils. This is because they may not know whether the pupil has taken a previous dose or whether the medication may interact with other medication being taken. If, however, the First Aider decides that the administration of pain relief will enable the student to remain at school there must be written or verbal consent from the parent.
In such cases a Parental Agreement Form (PAF1) (see “Electronic Forms for Parents” below) should be completed and returned for the attention of “St John’s First Aider”. Please ensure that the child has been given the stated medication without any adverse reaction in the past. In addition, it is essential that you are confident that the student is able to give accurate information to the First Aider of any medications they have taken already on that day. You will always be informed on the same day, when such medication has been given either by details written in the planner or on an administration slip, if the student does not have their planner to hand.
Some parents may decide that their child is responsible enough to carry their own pain relieving medication. In such instances, a child should carry a single dose of medication, for their own use in their school bags. Consideration should be given to the choice of analgesia. A child under 16 should never be given aspirin unless prescribed. If the student suffers from pain and regularly takes medication, medical advice should be sought.
As with any medication, records must be kept of when pain relief has been administered. The agreement forms and medication will be stored and locked in the First Aid room, reviewed annually and destroyed once the student has left the school.
Prescribed medication
Very few medicines need to be taken during school hours and in most cases, the appropriate dosage of medicine can be “three times a day”, and can be administered before and after school.
If prescribed medications need to be administered during the school day, then please complete a Parental Agreement for School to Administer Prescribed Medication Form (PAF2) (see “Electronic Forms for Parents” below) and return for the attention of the St John’s First Aider. Medicines must be in the pharmacist’s original container, clearly labelled with the student’s name and the dosage instructions.
Students requiring controlled drugs will not be able to carry their own medication, as this type of medication has to be kept in a locked cupboard. Please contact the First Aider to discuss.
Medication and residential trips
Excluding emergency and ADHD medication, students are responsible for administering their own medications. Please ensure the medication is in its original packaging and they take as prescribed. If for any reason this is not appropriate please contact the First Aider to discuss in advance of the trip.
Asthma
Asthmatic students must carry their inhalers at all times or leave them with a designated adult during PE lessons. We hold emergency spacers and Salbutamol for use in an emergency. If you would like the academy First Aider to hold detailed information regarding your son or daughter’s condition, please print and complete the Asthma Card (see Downloads below) and return for the attention of the St John’s First Aider.
For a copy of our Asthma Policy, please see Medical Policy Downloads below.
Severe allergic reactions (Anaphylaxis)
Students requiring Emergency medication for Anaphylaxis will have their Individual Health Care plan stored in the First Aid Room. Students who have been prescribed an EPIPEN / JEXT must carry their two devices with them at all times. These must be taken on day, residential trips and sports fixtures.
From 1 October 2017 the Human Medicines Regulations 2017 allow all schools to buy adrenaline auto-injector (AAI) devices without a prescription, for emergency use in children who are at risk of anaphylaxis if their own device is not available or not working (e.g. because it is broken, or out-of-date). We now store an Emergency anaphylaxis kit (Epipens 300mgs) for use in emergencies. It is imperative that the school is notified if your prescription is different for any reason. Please refer to the medical conditions policy for further details.
We currently have several students at St John’s who have severe allergic reaction to nuts and other products. The allergy to nuts is the most common high risk allergen and, as such, we would request that students do not come to St John’s with lunches that contain whole nuts or nut spreads, for example, peanut butter or similar nut based spread, or bars that contain nuts, in order to help minimise the unlikely risk that these children may accidentally come into contact with nuts and suffer a severe allergic reaction.
Please refer to the schools Allergens Policy (see Downloads below) for further details.
Epilepsy medication
Students who have epilepsy rescue medication will have an Individual Health Care Plan and medication stored in the First Aid Room. Please ensure the medication is within date and any changes to the care plan or medication is communicated to the St John’s First Aider.
Diabetes
Students that have diabetes will have their Individual Health Care Plan supplied by their diabetes specialist team. Your son or daughter will have space to store additional kit and emergency supplies within the First Aid room. Please keep the First Aider informed of any developments or changes to treatment as required.
Please do not hesitate to contact the St John’s First Aider to discuss any issues relating to the health and wellbeing of the students.
If you would like further information, please refer to The Medical Conditions policies available on our Policies & Finance page (in the About Us drop-down menu in the vertical navigation on the left).
